title: MSA §5.3 vendor-disclosure records — re-filing of W012297
summary:
A re-filing of W012297-030826 covering MSA §5.3 vendor-disclosure records:

- notifications from Flock to SMPD about §5.3 disclosures,
- SMPD records monitoring or tracking such disclosures,
- SMPD/Flock communications about §5.3 scope (including any review under AG Bulletin 2023-DLE-06), and
- any analysis or memorandum considering §5.3 alongside Civil Code §1798.90.55(b).

Includes scope clarifications intended to reduce review volume by identifying non-responsive record types.

policy_promises.quote: Flock may disclose Customer Data as required to provide the Services
policy_promises.tests: What records reflect Flock's exercise of §5.3, and SMPD's awareness of any such disclosure?

policy_promises.quote: ALPR information shall not be sold, shared, or transferred except to another public agency
directing law enforcement agencies to review vendor agreements for provisions allowing access beyond California public agencies
policy_promises.tests: What records reflect the AG-directed review?

prior_pra_refs.note: The original request was filed 2026-03-08 and closed on 2026-05-06 by consolidation into W012462-040226's email corpus. This re-filing covers the substantive questions on a clean docket.
W012462 was withdrawn 2026-05-06; the original consolidation into that request is no longer in effect.

filed_because: Re-files the substantive §5.3 questions after the original consolidation target was withdrawn. Asks the Department to treat the re-filing with corresponding urgency given the time elapsed since the original filing on 2026-03-08.
notes:
Initial response 2026-05-14; requester sent 2026-05-21 follow-up with four clarifying questions (search scope, per-item determinations, timeliness under §7922.535, and whether the 211,872-document email query reflects a search not limited to responsive records).

2026-05-28 response (Juliana Santiago, Management Analyst): Item 4 (legal review of §5.3 consistency with Civil Code §1798.90.55(b)) denied under Gov. Code §7927.705 / Evidence Code §954 (attorney-client privilege). For the remainder, the City states 'a good faith and diligent search yielded no records responsive to your request' while simultaneously releasing records on a rolling basis and promising a further response no later than 2026-06-11 — the same 'no responsive records' + rolling-production framing tracked in the disclosure-failure pattern. Not closed; still in rolling production.

2026-06-10 response (Juliana Santiago, Management Analyst): re-confirms Item 4 (City Attorney legal review of §5.3 vs Civil Code §1798.90.55(b)) denied under Gov. Code §7927.705 / Evidence Code §954 (attorney-client privilege). For the remainder, again states 'a good faith and diligent search yielded no records responsive' while continuing rolling production and pushing the next promised update to no later than 2026-06-24. Still not closed.

2026-06-24 response (Juliana Santiago, Management Analyst): the same pattern a third time — Item 4 (City Attorney legal review of §5.3 vs Civil Code §1798.90.55(b)) denied under Gov. Code §7927.705 / Evidence Code §954 (attorney-client privilege); for the remainder, again 'a good faith and diligent search yielded no records responsive' while continuing rolling production and pushing the next promised update to no later than 2026-07-08. Still not closed.

Pairs with W012683-050626, which isolates the monitoring-mechanism question (W012297 Item 6) into a single record category.
